observation.visible_scene: Against a plain gray studio background, a white-haired, bearded man in glasses and a gray suit stands on the right, holding an open spiral notebook and reading it with his left hand. On the left, a dark-gray articulated robot arm with a silver camera-like module and a glowing green ring at its wrist joint grips a white mug by its handle, holding it out toward the man.
visible_changes: At the start the man's right hand is not raised into view; from about t=0.24 to t=0.40 it rises above the top edge of the notebook, fingers gesturing.
From about t=0.48 to t=0.72 the man's right hand moves leftward toward the mug and comes into contact with it, resting on the mug/handle alongside the robot's gripper.
From t=0.72 through the end of the clip (t=3.20) the man's right hand stays on the mug while he continues to look down at and hold the notebook.

Throughout the clip the robot arm gradually extends horizontally: the span between its elbow cap and the mug increases, so the mug shifts slightly rightward (closer to the man), while the robot's gripper never releases the handle.
The green indicator ring on the robot's wrist is brightly lit in most frames but appears dim or off in a few middle frames (roughly t=1.84-2.24).
The man's head/torso and the robot base both drift a few pixels within the frame over the clip, consistent with a slight camera shift, though this is not separable from object motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the man ultimately takes the mug from the robot or the robot later releases it, since the gripper still holds the handle at the last frame.
What prompted the man's right hand to rise, and any action before t=0 or after t=3.20.
Whether the brief dimming of the green wrist ring reflects a real state change of the robot or is a rendering/compression artifact.
uncertain_details: Camera motion vs. subject motion is hard to disambiguate because the background is featureless; only the robot-internal elbow-to-mug extension is camera-independent.
Exact moment of first hand-mug contact (between t=0.64 and t=0.72) is approximate.
The green-ring 'off' interval is inferred from low-contrast frames and may be inconsistent.
